newsitem.title: USA: Most power service in NYC area restored.
newsitem.headline: Most power service in NYC area restored.

text.p: Most electricity customers in the greater New York City metropolitan area saw their service restored Friday morning after heavy winds Thursday caused widespread outages throughout eastern U.S.
"We have been able to restore a majority of the power," said a spokeswoman for Long Island Lighting Co (LILCO).
The utility said 71,750 of its customers lost power due to gusty conditions that resulted in broken tree limbs falling on overhead power lines.
As of 1130 EST, only 300 customers in central Nassau and western Suffolk counties were still without electricity, the LILCO spokeswoman said.
LILCO supplies electricity to 1.1 million customers on Long Island.

Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc (ConEd) said it restored power to nearly 12,500 customers in New York City and suburban Westchester County, just north of city, who experienced power loss yesterday, a ConEd spokesman said.
Nearby counties in New Jersey and Connecticut also reported thousands of customers whose service was disrupted because of downed distribution lines.
